title: The dth Fitting ideal detects smoothness in a pure-dimensional flat family
statement: Let $g:T\to B$ be a flat morphism of schemes [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and let $d\geq0$ be an integer. Assume every nonempty geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] is equidimensional of dimension $d$ [def-weil-pure-dimension]. Write $\Omega^1_{T/B}$ for the relative differential sheaf [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf]. Let $Z_d\hookrightarrow T$ be the closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion] cut out by $\operatorname{Fit}_d(\Omega^1_{T/B})$: on an affine chart with generators $\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_n$ of the differential module and relation module $K\subset A^n$, this is the ideal generated by the $(n-d)\times(n-d)$ minors of matrices with rows in $K$; for $d\geq n$ it is the unit ideal. These ideals do not depend on the chosen generators and commute with localization [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change], so they glue to the ideal sheaf $\operatorname{Fit}_d(\Omega^1_{T/B})$; for $d=1$ this is [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme]. Then the locus $V\subseteq T$ of points $x$ at which $g$ is smooth, i.e. having an open neighbourhood $U$ with $g|_U$ smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], is open, and $|Z_d|=|T|\setminus V$.

source.place: Tag 0C3K (lemma-d-fitting-ideal-omega-smooth); geometric-fibre formulation using Algebra Tag 00P4 (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-preserved-field-extension) to identify the pure fibre dimension; Fitting convention from More on Algebra Tags 07Z8 and 07ZA

proof.text: Locally of finite presentation implies that on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$ over an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq B$ the $R$-algebra $A$ is finitely generated, so $\Omega_{A/R}$ is generated by the differentials of finitely many algebra generators; hence $\Omega^1_{T/B}$ is a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_T$-module and $\operatorname{Fit}_d(\Omega^1_{T/B})$ is its $d$-th Fitting ideal sheaf in the sense of [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-generate-locally]. Clause (2) of that lemma, applied with $S=T$, $\mathcal F=\Omega^1_{T/B}$ and $r=d$, says that for every $x\in T$: $x\notin|Z_d|$ if and only if the stalk $\Omega^1_{T/B,x}$ is generated by at most $d$ elements over $\mathcal O_{T,x}$. The set $T\setminus|Z_d|$ is open because $Z_d$ is a closed subscheme.

source.place: Tag 0C3F, Tag 05P8 and More on Algebra Tag 07ZC (3), applied to F = Omega^1_{T/B}

Fix $x\in T$, put $s=g(x)$, and let $ ar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega	o B$, $\Omega=\overline{\kappa(s)}$, be the geometric point of the geometric fibre $T_{ ar s}=T	imes_B\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Choose affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A
i x$ of $T$ and $\operatorname{Spec}R
i s$ of $B$ with $g(\operatorname{Spec}A)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$; then $C=A\otimes_R\kappa(s)$ is a finite type $\kappa(s)$-algebra, $\operatorname{Spec}C$ is an open neighbourhood of $x$ in the fibre $T_s$, and $\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\Omega)$ is the open preimage of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ in $T_{ ar s}$. Since $\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\Omega
eq0$ it has a prime ideal, giving a point $ ar x\in\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\Omega)$ over $x$; in particular $T_{ ar s}$ is nonempty, hence of pure dimension $d$ [def-weil-pure-dimension] by hypothesis. The morphism $T_{ ar s}	o\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is locally of finite presentation, being a base change of $g$ (clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]), so locally of finite type, and [lem-sbc-equidimensional-open-local-dimension] (with $Y=O=T_{ ar s}$, $n=d$) gives $\dim_{ ar x}T_{ ar s}=d$. The dimension at a point is computed on any open neighbourhood (its defining minimum runs over arbitrarily small opens), so $\dim_{ ar x}\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\Omega)=d$; by [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-field-extension] (with $k=\kappa(s)$, $K=\Omega$, $S=C$) this equals $\dim_x\operatorname{Spec}C=\dim_x(T_s)$. Hence $\dim_x(T_{g(x)})=d$ for every $x\in T$.

source.place: Tag 0C3K hypothesis (3) in its geometric-fibre form, with Varieties Tag 0A21 (3),(5) for the pointwise dimension and Algebra Tag 00P4 for the field extension

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-smooth-at-point-differential-criterion] to $g$ at $x$: $g$ is locally of finite presentation by hypothesis, the local ring map $\mathcal O_{B,g(x)}\to\mathcal O_{T,x}$ is flat because $g$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], and the fibre dimension $\dim_x(T_{g(x)})$ in that criterion is $d$ by Step 2. Therefore $g$ is smooth at $x$ if and only if $\Omega^1_{T/B,x}$ is generated by at most $d$ elements.

source.place: Tag 01V9, equivalence (1) and (3), applied with the dimension from Step 2

proof.text: By Steps 1 and 3, for every $x\in T$: $g$ is smooth at $x$ if and only if $\Omega^1_{T/B,x}$ is generated by at most $d$ elements if and only if $x\notin|Z_d|$. Thus $V=|T|\setminus|Z_d|$, which is open by Step 1, and $|Z_d|=|T|\setminus V$. When $d=1$ the ideal $\operatorname{Fit}_1(\Omega^1_{T/B})$ is by definition the ideal of [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme], so $Z_1=\operatorname{Sing}(g)$.

lean.statement: theorem dthFitting_smoothLocus {T B : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ B) (d : ℕ) [Flat g] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation g] (hpure : ∀ b : B, (pullback g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (B.residueField b) (AlgebraicClosure (B.residueField b)))) ≫ B.fromSpecResidueField b)).IsPureDimension d) : ∃ V : Set T, IsOpen V ∧ (∀ x : T, x ∈ V ↔ ∃ U : T.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ Smooth (U.ι ≫ g)) ∧ ((Scheme.Modules.fittingIdealSheaf g.relativeDifferentials d).support : Set T) = Set.univ \ V ∧ (d = 1 → Scheme.Modules.fittingIdealSheaf g.relativeDifferentials 1 = Scheme.firstFittingIdealSheaf g)
